definitions.explanation: A black-and-white mammal of the Americas that sprays a foul-smelling liquid when threatened.

examples.japanese: スカンク⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦ひどい→ひどい：01097_hidoi⟧におい⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{出|だ}す→出す：01087_dasu⟧。
examples.english: Skunks give off a terrible smell.
The dog got sprayed by a skunk.

examples.japanese: スカンク⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{危険|きけん}→危険：01141_kiken⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{感|かん}じる→感じる：02044_kanjiru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧、⟦{尾|お}→尾：01898_o⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{上|あ}げて→上げる：02443_ageru⟧⟦{相手|あいて}→相手：01677_aite⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{向|む}かって→向かう：01186_mukau⟧⟦{液|えき}→液：02270_eki⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{噴射|ふんしゃ}→噴射：15045_funsha⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: When it senses danger, a skunk raises its tail and sprays its foe.

notes:
USAGE:
- Not native to Japan; most Japanese know it from cartoons and zoos, and スカンク is used jokingly of anything (or anyone) that smells.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- スカンク⟦の→の：09472_no⟧におい / {臭|にお}い: the smell of a skunk
- ⟦{液|えき}→液：02270_eki⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{噴射|ふんしゃ}→噴射：15045_funsha⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to spray the liquid

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦イタチ→イタチ：23835_itachi⟧: weasel — native to Japan, also known for a bad-smelling spray in a pinch (⟦イタチ→イタチ：23835_itachi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{最後|さいご}っ{屁|ぺ})
